children: UAE-based AMEA Power has started commercial operations at its $27 million, 24-megawatt-peak (MWp) Ituka solar photovoltaic (PV) project in Uganda.

The project, located in Uleppi in Madi Okollo District in West Nile region, reached commercial operations date (COD) following the completion of reliability and performance tests, the company said in a statement.
The milestone follows the energisation in July 2026 of the project's 25-megavolt-ampere (MVA), 132/33-kilovolt (kV) substation to enable clean electricity supply to the national grid.
Uganda Electricity Transmission Company Limited (UETCL) is the project's offtaker.
The solar plant is being developed through Ituka West Nile Uganda Limited, a Uganda-registered project company wholly owned by AMEA Power.

The facility is expected to generate approximately 53,940 megawatt-hours (MWh) of electricity annually and supply power equivalent to the needs of more than 192,640 households, while avoiding an estimated 26,600 tonnes of carbon emissions per year, according to the statement.

The project was financed through a mix of debt and equity from AMEA Power and the Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF), a Private Infrastructure Development Group (PIDG) company, managed by Ninety One.

The statement didn’t specify the debt-equity split, power purchase agreement tariff or tenor, or EPC contractor details, but in November 2024, EAAIF had announced it brought AMEA Power’s 20 MW solar PV plant in north-western Uganda to financial close investing nearly $18 million in the project.
The Ituka project is AMEA Power's first operational asset in Uganda.
(Writing by SA Kader; Editing by Anoop Menon)
